title: To find out what customers think, this $2bn startup asks their AI twins
excerpt: A startup wants companies to stop asking real people what they think, and ask fake ones instead. Simile has raised $200m at a $2bn valuation to build “agentic twins,” AI stand-ins for real consumers that firms can survey by the million.
content_html:
A startup wants companies to stop asking real people what they think, and ask fake ones instead. Simile has raised $200m at a $2bn valuation to build “agentic twins,” AI stand-ins for real consumers that firms can survey by the million.

Greenoaks led the round, the New York Times reported, with Index Ventures and others returning. It is a fast turn. The year-old startup raised $100m less than six months ago.

Surveying people who do not exist

Simile’s pitch is that it can predict how people will behave by simulating them. Companies use it to test a new product or gauge how a brand lands, faster and cheaper than a traditional market-research study.

The customers are real even if the respondents are not. Last autumn, CVS Health used 400,000 agentic twins to work out how to get patients to take their medicine. Deloitte and the finance app Wealthfront are clients too.

“If you’re able to simulate the world, you can basically test out countless interventions,” said Joon Sung Park, Simile’s 32-year-old chief executive. He called it “a window into humanity.”

Real humans built the fake ones

The founders come straight from the research that started this field. Park built Simile from a 2023 Stanford paper on AI agents that mimic human life, a kind of AI version of The Sims. His co-founders include Percy Liang, who helped coin the term “foundation model.”

The model itself started with real people. Simile ran two-hour interviews with 1,000 representative participants, then teamed with Gallup to add input from a few million more. It claims its answers are 85% to 99% accurate, depending on the group.

Pricing follows the crowd. Simile charges partly by how many agents it models, from hundreds of thousands to millions. “The larger the panel, the higher the price,” Park said.

A bold, unproven idea

The premise is contested. Those accuracy figures are Simile’s own, and whether AI stand-ins truly capture how humans behave is exactly what critics doubt. Rivals such as Helm, Artificial Societies and Aaru are chasing the same idea, part of the wider hunt for measurable value from AI.

There is irony in it, too. Simile leans on real human data to manufacture the fake kind. It does so on a web already flooding with AI agents, where proving you are a real person is its own business. Its stated goal, per Pulse 2.0, is to model all eight billion people on earth. It is the sort of promise enterprise buyers will judge on results.

content_html_zh:
一家初创公司希望公司不要再询问真实的人的想法，而是询问虚假的人。 Simile 已以 20 亿美元的估值筹集了 2 亿美元，用于打造“代理双胞胎”，即真实消费者的人工智能替身，企业可以对数百万消费者进行调查。

据《纽约时报》报道，Greenoaks 领投了本轮融资，Index Ventures 和其他公司也回归。 这是一个快速转弯。 这家成立一年的初创公司在不到六个月前筹集了 1 亿美元。

调查不存在的人

Simile 的宣传是，它可以通过模拟人们来预测他们的行为方式。 公司用它来测试新产品或衡量品牌的落地情况，比传统的市场研究更快、更便宜。

即使受访者不是真实的，客户也是真实的。 去年秋天，CVS Health 使用 400,000 名药剂双胞胎来研究如何让患者服药。 德勤和金融应用 Wea​​lthfront 也是客户。

Simile 32 岁的首席执行官 Joon Sung Park 表示：“如果你能够模拟这个世界，你基本上就可以测试无数的干预措施。” 他称之为“了解人性的窗口”。

真人建造了假人

创始人直接来自该领域的研究。 Park 根据 2023 年斯坦福大学一篇关于模仿人类生活的人工智能代理的论文构建了 Simile，这是《模拟人生》的人工智能版本。 他的联合创始人包括珀西·梁 (Percy Liang)，他帮助创造了“基础模型”一词。

该模型本身是从真人开始的。 Simile 对 1,000 名参与者代表进行了两个小时的采访，然后与盖洛普合作收集了数百万人的意见。 它声称其答案的准确率是 85% 到 99%，具体取决于群体。

定价随大众而定。 Simile 部分收费是根据其代理的代理数量来收费，从数十万到数百万不等。 “面板越大，价格就越高，”帕克说。

一个大胆的、未经证实的想法

前提是有争议的。 这些准确度数据是 Simile 自己的，而人工智能替身是否真正捕捉到了人类的行为方式正是批评者所怀疑的。 Helm、Artificial Societies 和 Aaru 等竞争对手也在追求同样的想法，这是更广泛地寻求人工智能可衡量价值的一部分。

其中也有讽刺意味。 Simile 依靠真实的人类数据来制造假货。 它是在一个已经充斥着人工智能代理的网络上做到这一点的，在网络上证明你是一个真实的人是它自己的事。 根据 Pulse 2.0，其既定目标是对地球上所​​有 80 亿人进行建模。 这是企业买家会根据结果进行判断的那种承诺。
